install: Needs Node 22+, Pi 1.4.x on `PATH` and Python 3.13+.
pi install git:github.com/Shredi/pi-foreman            # global; pin with @<tag-or-commit>
/foreman setup --dry-run   # inside Pi: show the planned changes, write nothing
bin/foreman setup          # from a checkout (or: node setup.mjs)

features.title: Package install, setup and checks
features.purpose: `foreman setup` migrates the keys of the removed permission package to `gate.*`, writes the generated `subagents` block and a starter `foreman.json`; `/foreman doctor` checks the result and `update-check` lists newer pinned packages.

features.title: Setup profiles and feature toggles
features.purpose: `foreman setup` applies a named profile (`orchestration`, `standard` or `full`) and per-feature toggles to the user `foreman.json` and records the choice; `foreman features` lists the state of every toggleable feature and the profile's deviations.

features.title: Providers line in doctor
features.purpose: `/foreman doctor` prints `providers: <list>`, the providers the model registry holds in this session; a missing `claude-bridge` there means the bridge is not loaded or has not registered yet (see the opened-session note).

features.title: Model map per provider and role
features.purpose: Maps each role to a model and thinking level per provider; until a model is mapped, children run on Pi's default model and an interactive session shows one notice.

features.title: Model presets
features.purpose: Opt-in model maps under `config/presets/` (role models, ranks, strong rungs, reviewer climb) merged into your `foreman.json` on request, never by default. The `inexpensive` preset names roles by rank tier and resolves them from your `providers.<x>.ranks` at apply time (docs/presets.md).

features.title: Role definitions
features.purpose: Per-role prompt file, appended prompt text, tool allowlist, launch mode and run-time default of the neutral roles; a launch timeoutMs wins, capped by ceremony.launchTimeoutCapMinutes. roles.<x>.mcp is the ceiling of MCP servers a child may load on demand through tool_search (a launch mcp field narrows it). mcp.directProviders lists the providers that fix a turn's tool list (default claude-bridge): a child on one gets its allowed deferred MCP tools declared before the first prompt.

features.title: Display names
features.purpose: Shows roles under a display-name preset (`classic` personal names, `plain` ids) or your own map; no code compares a display name.

features.title: Codemode per role
features.purpose: Gives a role the `codemode` tool, whose script calls each pass the guards and permissions on their own (on for the foreman and explorer by default).

features.title: Role ladder (strong rung and climbs)
features.purpose: A child climbs to its role's strong model through the foreman after a context, turns, stuck or review-FAIL handoff; with no strong rung mapped nothing climbs.

features.title: Idle model downshift
features.purpose: A notice turn (child, wake, intercom, other) that starts on a cold cache runs on the foreman's idle rung; the owner's next input restores the base model. With no idle rung mapped nothing changes.

features.title: Rank policy for child models
features.purpose: Ranks models into tiers so children may only launch below (or at) the foreman's tier; with no ranks anywhere the policy does nothing.

features.title: Reviewer climb
features.purpose: Sends the next reviewer launch to its strong rung after a second FAIL of one ledger item, and to a security rung on a security-shaped diff.

features.title: Review panel shadows
features.purpose: Adds shadow reviewer models beside the primary on the named occasions; their findings are reported but never block, mark items or satisfy the PR gate.

features.title: Different-model rule for reviews
features.purpose: Moves a reviewer launch off the foreman's own model to the next differing rung, else to `ceremony.reviewModel`.

features.title: Per-occasion review overrides
features.purpose: Sets the thinking level and/or model of a reviewer launch per occasion (`item`, `plan-review`, `pre-pr`, `second-opinion`).

features.title: Self-planning at heavy
features.purpose: `ceremony.planner: self` (default): the foreman writes the heavy plan itself and its approved checkpoint satisfies the planner step; `role` keeps the planner launch and falls back to `self` when the planner's rank is not below the foreman's.

features.title: Plan checkpoint verdict by parent file
features.purpose: A session opened with a parent takes the plan checkpoint verdict from the parent-written `ruling-plan.md` (APPROVED, REVISE <text> or REJECT) instead of a dialog; plan state, the user tier and the plan phase (`/foreman plan`, `--plan-first`) survive `/reload` and resume; `human` keeps the dialog for an attended session.

features.title: Plan review below heavy
features.purpose: Refuses the owner checkpoint until a `[plan-review]` reviewer verdict exists for the current plan version (the body above any ruling, decision-log or addendum appendix, so an appended ruling needs no new review); on for heavy by default, opt-in for trivial and standard.

features.title: Findings store and reviewer model stats
features.purpose: Records every reviewer run's located findings locally, with `foreman findings` to list, dismiss or export them and `foreman retro models` to compare reviewer models.

features.title: Benchmark
features.purpose: Measures harness changes over Harbor tasks in local Docker, and reviewer models over planted-defect diffs with `foreman bench review`.

features.title: Bench climb policies
features.purpose: Explores cheap-to-strong reviewer climb policies offline over review-bench cells; the runtime has no climb on a finding.

features.title: Tiers and finish gates
features.purpose: The foreman records a tier (trivial, standard, heavy) that the adapter checks, and may only finish once the tier's required steps and review gate are met, or when the session changed nothing (no builder run, no foreman edit, a clean work tree).

features.title: Read budgets
features.purpose: Reminds the foreman to delegate once its own reads pass a budget (never refuses a read; coordination calls do not count), caps rechecks after a PASS (a plan-review PASS does not start the recheck window), and gives child roles their own read budgets.

features.title: Launch wait and fan-out
features.purpose: Returns a foreman launch at once with its receipt (the completion notice starts the next turn; "block" holds it until the child ends, for replay rigs and bench), drops duplicate completion notices and caps concurrent children.

features.title: Long waits
features.purpose: The foreman-only `foreman_wait` tool waits on timers, files, processes and CI runs within a duration and concurrency limit, batching its notices.

features.title: Background shell runs
features.purpose: The foreman-only `foreman_bg` tool starts a shell command detached, logs to the session scratch dir and registers a pid wait with your note; it passes the same bash guards as the foreground tool.

features.title: Background-tasks add-on detection
features.purpose: Detects the optional pi-background-tasks add-on (install with `pi install npm:pi-background-tasks@2.6.10` on consent via `foreman setup --addon background-tasks`; set `PI_BG_FEATURES=process` in the shell profile so it is present when Pi starts): `/foreman doctor` reports it, `foreman_bg` defers to its `bg_run` tool, `/foreman waits` lists its tasks and `bg_run` passes the same bash guards. Nothing requires it.

features.title: Orientation packet
features.purpose: Adds a short repository overview (file tree, AGENTS.md or README head, build and test commands) to the foreman's system prompt once per session.

features.title: Child scratch dirs
features.purpose: Gives every single-child launch its own temp dir (`$FOREMAN_SCRATCH`) that the guards allow writes in and the harness removes when the run ends.

features.title: Permission policy
features.purpose: Your own policy file (`gate.policy.userFile`, default `<agentDir>/pi-foreman/policy.md`) and an overlay's `safety.policy.files` add allow, deny and ask entries on top of the shipped policy, judged by the gate's review model; a project file can only add deny and ask entries.

features.title: Reads of Pi's install and run dirs
features.purpose: Shell reads (`ls`, `cat`) of Pi's own install releases and the pi-subagents run root need no dialog; the gate's path rules compute them at runtime from the session's roots.

features.title: Own CLI allow
features.purpose: The foreman session's own `bin/foreman` (explicit path, realpath inside its root) with `session open|brief|list`, `dialogs` or `findings list` is allowed before the review model (trace `overlay_allow{rule: own_cli}`); children and forwarded asks, shell control, `VAR=`, `..` or a symlink out, and user ask/deny rules keep the normal path.

features.title: Permission auto-review
features.purpose: The gate's review model judges every call no floor or default decides, against the merged policy; unset, it picks the inexpensive rung of the role map, and with none the call asks you.

features.title: Child asks to the parent
features.purpose: A subagent child's plain policy ask goes to its parent's pane (`gate.childAsk`, `parent` by default); `deny` denies it with a text naming what to report, and a timeout (`gate.askTimeoutMs`) denies too. A headless session always denies an ask.

features.title: Review critic questions
features.purpose: Every reviewer and senior-reviewer task carries the `review.critic` questions (default: four lean/friction/dispensable/direction questions) and the instruction to answer each once per ledger item as a `CRITIC: <item> Q<k>: <answer>` line; the harness does not parse the lines.

features.title: Git guard and PR gate
features.purpose: Lints the foreman's commits and pushes (protected branches, message pattern, trailers, an optional check command) and refuses a PR without a reviewer PASS on the current head.

features.title: Git tool pack
features.purpose: Structured, capped git read tools (git_status, git_log, git_diff_stat, git_branch_state) for the foreman and for children with bash; the checked move, copy and worktree-remove tools count as pack members in the trace.

features.title: PR tools
features.purpose: Host-neutral pull request tools (pr_create, pr_status, pr_checks, pr_comments, pr_watch, pr_track, pr_untrack): the foreman opens a PR after a reviewer PASS and a watch wakes it when checks finish or a comment lands. Pushed, searched, acted-on and touched PRs are tracked by host, owner, repo and number, shown in a PR widget above the editor and, with the shared watch, with review requests and failing bot PRs.

features.title: External sidebar status
features.purpose: Runs a command you configure on an interval and shows its JSON items (label and state) as extra dots on the Herdr sidebar; the items are display data only, the program must lie outside the workspace, and the setting is read from user or overlay config only.

features.title: Children may push
features.purpose: Lets subagent children push; by default they may commit but never push, and they never open PRs.

features.title: Review required before close-out
features.purpose: Requires a review before close-out in every session.

features.title: Workflow scripts and schedules
features.purpose: Lets the foreman run pi-subagents workflow scripts and `schedule.*` calls, which can launch any agent outside the role map; they stay refused at tier heavy.

features.title: Guards and safe operations
features.purpose: Loads the guard extensions into every child, sets the limits of the precondition-checked copy and worktree-remove tools, and picks the Python that runs every guard.

features.title: Claude bridge isolation
features.purpose: With the Claude bridge, points `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` at an empty folder so the host's Claude Code settings, hooks and plugins do not load into bridge turns. `bridge.promptCacheTtl` sets Claude Code's prompt-cache TTL for bridge turns: 1h for the foreman, 5m for subagents.

features.title: Opened sessions over pi-intercom
features.purpose: `/foreman session` opens a second pi-foreman session on a brief (in a Herdr tab or a printed command), briefs it and closes it over the bundled pi-intercom. The session runs on the `session-foreman` role's model (default: the opening session's own model) and never on a higher rank.

features.title: herdr-app and herdr-core sessions (experimental)
features.purpose: Inside an herdr-app terminal (`HC_TERMINAL_ID` set), `foreman session open` can run the child with `hc run`, nested under the parent terminal; presence files record the terminal id so a viewer can join them. `--no-notify` is always passed, so hc never types a child's notes into the parent, and `--keep` is always passed, so the child survives core loss and reboot (in its own tab when the opener's terminal carries `herdr.space`). `sessions.backend` picks herdr, hc or the printed command (default `auto`); `sessions.hc.outliveParent` (default true) lets a child outlive its parent terminal. User or overlay config only.

features.title: Round worktree for a session open
features.purpose: `foreman session open <label> <brief> --worktree [--base REF]` (and `foreman_session_open` with `worktree: true`) creates the session's own linked worktree at `<close.worktreeDir>/<label>` on the branch `<prefix>/<label>` from the fetched default branch, installs dependencies with `npm ci` only when a lockfile is declared, and opens the session there. `sessions.worktree.branchPrefix` (default `round`) sets the prefix. User or overlay config only.

features.title: Open PRs in radar and the herdr-app mod
features.purpose: When enabled, the extension searches GitHub through `gh` (at most every `radar.openPrs.refreshSeconds`, default 900) for your open PRs, those with your review requested (`mine`) and those of configured bot `authors` inside `scope`, and caches them on disk. `foreman radar --json` reports them as `openPrs` for the Open PRs section of the herdr-app mod; radar polls never call the network. Off by default. User or overlay config only.

features.title: Remote child sessions over SSH
features.purpose: `foreman session open --machine <name>` opens a child session on a machine saved in Herdr and listed in `sessions.machines`, over SSH. By default (`returnPath` `pull`) the child appends its notices to an outbox file on that machine and the parent fetches them over its own SSH call, so the remote never connects back; `push` sends them by cross-machine pi-intercom notices instead. The parent mirrors the notices into files. `foreman session close-remote` (and `/foreman close`) closes such a child over the same SSH call. User or overlay config only.

features.title: Reload-safe round state
features.purpose: In a round session with `PI_FOREMAN_HANDOFF_DIR` set, `<handoff dir>/round-state.json` keeps the checkpointed plan's topic and hash, its plan-review verdict and counters, so `/reload` keeps them. It never keeps an approval: the checkpoint approval returns from the session's own state entry, or from the parent's `ruling-plan.md` or `ruling.md` newer than both the plan and the handoff plan.

features.title: Remote intercom
features.purpose: Allows intercom across machines and opening panes; both are off by default.

features.title: Repository sync
features.purpose: `/sync` runs the retro, then pulls, commits (explicit paths only) and pushes the repositories you list, and prints the CLOSE report; it does nothing until you list one.
features.enable: {"sync": {"repos": [{"path": "<absolute path of a repository you trust>", "branch": "main", "paths": ["<glob of paths to sync>"]}]}}

features.title: Retro and backlog
features.purpose: `/retro` prints the session's friction metrics, writes permission-allow proposals and files findings to a local backlog read with `foreman backlog`.

features.title: Repository backlog
features.purpose: Moves the central retro backlog elsewhere or sends a workspace's findings into its own `.workflow/retro-backlog.md`, optionally committed by `/sync`.

features.title: Session close and cleanup
features.purpose: Records what a session creates, prints a CLOSE report and removes its own worktrees and scratch only when every precondition passes.

features.title: Trace
features.purpose: Writes allowlisted trace records per session and child (no command lines or file contents); by default it follows the effective retro switch.

features.title: Usage footer and children widget
features.purpose: Shows tokens, list-price cost and child launches in the footer, the children widget below the editor and the glyph set, with `/foreman cost` for a summary.

features.title: Permission dialogs as a tool and CLI
features.purpose: The foreman-only `foreman_dialogs({trace?})` tool and `foreman dialogs <trace>` (`bin/foreman`, `.cmd`, `.ps1`) return the JSON of `/foreman dialogs --json` for this session's trace or a named trace file; read only. A session's own async run results join the read-only verbs.

features.title: Structured in-pane question
features.purpose: The foreman-only `ask_user_question({questions})` tool (1 to 4 questions, 2 to 4 options each plus free text) raises the questions in the pane and blocks the turn until a human answers; without a UI it tells the agent to use the ask.md file path, which stays unchanged. With an open ask.md in a handoff dir where the session is the child the answer is also written to `ruling-<n>.md`.

features.title: Gate review and dialog
features.purpose: The gate decides every tool call: floors and defaults first, then self-modification rules (a dialog by rule, never model-cleared), then the review model against the policy. An allow continues, a deny is final, an ask or an unreachable review opens the owner dialog (a round session files ask.md; children and headless sessions are denied with what to report).

features.title: Herdr pane state
features.purpose: In a Herdr pane, shows any open dialog or permission ask as blocked and tags opened child and parent panes.

features.title: Radar
features.purpose: `foreman radar` shows a live tree of the running pi-foreman sessions and their children from presence files.

features.title: Compaction cap
features.purpose: Caps the context size at which Pi's own auto-compaction fires: `foreman setup` writes a per-model point (a price-tier boundary minus headroom, or this cap) as Pi's compaction.modelOverrides. The idle warm compaction and the footer context bar use the same point.

features.title: Host pressure gate
features.purpose: Samples load, free memory and free disk; at high pressure child launches run one at a time and the strong climb pauses, at critical pressure launches are deferred until the host recovers (10 minutes at most). `/foreman doctor` prints the current level and `/foreman status` the last sample.

features.title: Idle prompt-cache policy
features.purpose: Per-provider prompt-cache TTL, billing and keep-alive so an idle session on a token-billed provider does not resume cold; on by default for claude-bridge through the built-in defaults (the claude-bridge TTL is derived from `bridge.promptCacheTtl`, 3600 s for the foreman and 300 s for subagents; the claude-bridge preset keeps the keep-alive on with awayTicks 2 and gives the foreman role an idle rung); github-copilot has built-in per-model TTLs for display only; off for request-billed providers; silent without an entry. A warm budget (half a cold re-cache per idle), a presence gate (warms while the owner is away are limited) and, for TTLs beyond Pi's 30-minute idle cap, warms sent by pi-foreman itself apply to the keep-alive.
features.enable: set providers.claude-bridge.cache.keepalive.enabled to false (off) or true (on) in user or overlay config, or foreman config apply-preset claude-bridge --dry-run   # or: {"providers": {"<provider>": {"cache": {"ttlSeconds": 300, "billing": "token", "keepalive": {"enabled": true}}}}}

overlayQuickStart.note: Map every role you use to a model per provider (or apply a preset first and adjust it).
Give the builder and reviewer a strong rung so the ladder has somewhere to climb.
pi-intercom ships with the package; keep it unless you set up with --no-intercom, and leave remote intercom off.
List the repositories `/sync` may pull, commit and push; user or overlay config only.
Point the retro backlog at a directory or repository store you keep; user or overlay config only.
Add a second vendor's model as a silent shadow before a PR; user or overlay config only.

invariants: One-way flow: an overlay consumes a pinned pi-foreman release and never patches the harness; nothing from an overlay is copied back into this repository.
Public-repo rule: pi-foreman is generic and public. Hosts, names, private paths and model-map details of one installation belong in that installation's overlay, never in this repository.
Tighten-only safety: the project and session layers may only make `safety.*` and the keys marked tighten-only stricter, so a cloned repository cannot loosen your guards.
Project trust: the project layer `.pi/foreman.json` is read only after Pi's project trust is resolved; project packages also load only after trust.
Role ids stay neutral (`foreman`, `planner`, `explorer`, `builder`, `reviewer`, `senior-reviewer`, `finalizer`); display names come only from config.
Setup owns the `subagents` block in `settings.json`: put your rules into `foreman.json` and your policy file, a hand edit of the generated block is overwritten.
Children never open PRs and reach the foreman through `contact_supervisor`, never through pi-intercom.
